description: The fleet's privileged verb set. An envelope grants capability over verbs from this table, never over prose. A verb absent from this table is unexpressible: it cannot be granted, denied, or argued — it traps to console (ENOSYS). Matching is mechanical, field-by-field against each verb's bounds signature; ambiguity is a non-match.
invariants: Envelopes cite verbs by id; free text never appears on the checking path.
The check is field-by-field validation of call args against envelope bounds. No interpretation. A near-miss is a fault (EAMBIG), not a stretch.
Editing this table is itself verb 11 (envelope.issue): root-only, operator-key gated, FRANK-recorded.
Every call — granted or faulted — writes a FRANK ledger entry: verb, args, envelope_id or errno. Grants and denials get the same ink.
enforcement=soft is a standing project to become hard. The table tracks which walls are real so a policy is never mistaken for a wall.

rings.root: The operator at the console. Sole issuer of envelopes and editor of this table. Not an agent.

unprivileged_floor.description: Ring-3 operations that never cross the syscall boundary. No envelope, no trap, no per-call ledger entry. Explicitly enumerated so the trap path stays quiet enough to be taken seriously.
operations: read: file reads, git log/diff/status, ledger_read, kb_search/kb_get, soil_get/soil_list/soil_search, handoff_latest, grove_get_history/grove_inbox
status: willow_status, fleet_status, dream_check, env_check, diagnostic_summary
compute: local inference that produces no side effect outside the session (infer_*, embedding, rendering)
own-namespace session state: handoff drafts, scratchpad writes, session anchors
unprivileged_floor.note: Anything not listed here and not in the table is ENOSYS, not implicitly unprivileged.

ENOSYS.meaning: Verb not in the table at all.
ENOSYS.note: This is how the table learns it is incomplete. Request attached verbatim.

ENOENT.meaning: Verb exists; no envelope covers this call.
ENOENT.note: Proposed action enqueued via human_required queue with the call args attached.

ENOGRANTS.meaning: The registry loaded but holds zero active grants — systemic, not a per-call miss.
ENOGRANTS.note: A functioning system always holds at least the orchestrator seat's own planting, so this is never steady state: an unpopulated starter, or (issue #332) the empty starter seeded at a relocated $WILLOW_HOME shadowing the ratified registry. Distinct from ENOENT so the systemic cause surfaces at the first check instead of reading as one grant expiring. The reason names the resolved registry file.

EACCES.meaning: A covering envelope exists but grantee or ring does not match.
EACCES.note: No trap. A wrong-ring request does not bother the console; the FRANK entry is the alarm.

EDQUOT.note: Intent was previously ratified; trap carries a pre-drafted renewal for one-decision remedy.

EAMBIG.meaning: Near-miss: nearest envelope matches on verb and grantee but fails one or more bound fields.
EAMBIG.note: Trap carries the field-level diff between the call and the nearest envelope. The remedy is the operator widening the envelope once — never the checker stretching it.

verbs.summary: Write access to a filesystem scope.
verbs.note: The MMU. Existing reach grants in pre-approved.json are envelopes over this verb.

verbs.summary: Create commits in a repository's local history.

bounds.branches: list[branch-glob] — e.g. feature/*, never a protected branch by glob accident

verbs.note: Local history only; leaving the machine is verb 3.

verbs.summary: Publish local history to a remote.

bounds.force: boolean — force-push must be granted explicitly, default false

verbs.note: First verb that leaves the box. Hard-enforcement path: org rulesets + machine identities after the GitHub-org migration.

verbs.summary: Open a pull request.
verbs.note: Cheap and reversible; bounds exist mainly so pr.open cannot target foreign repos.

verbs.summary: Merge a pull request into a base branch.

bounds.requires_ci: boolean — green CI as a precondition, checked not asserted

verbs.note: The flagship case: Dual Commit's second signature. Hard path: org ruleset requiring the envelope id in the merge commit message.

verbs.summary: Execute shell work in a sandbox profile.

bounds.sandbox_profile: profile id — binds, net, credentials are properties of the profile, not the call

verbs.enforced_by: Kart daemon + bwrap — all agent shell is already mediated
verbs.note: allow_net / allow_localhost / detached are profile dimensions. An unsandboxed shell is not a wider bound; it is ENOSYS.

verbs.summary: Outbound read-only network retrieval.

bounds.read_only: always true — a writing request is verb 8 or ENOSYS

verbs.enforced_by: partially — Kart allow_net gate exists but is binary, not domain-scoped
verbs.note: Hard path: domain allowlist in the sandbox network namespace.

verbs.summary: Post to an internal fleet channel.
verbs.note: Internal only. Pull channel history before posting remains law regardless of envelope.

verbs.summary: Send anything to a human-facing or third-party surface: email, Discord to humans, issue comments on foreign repos, any publish.
verbs.note: Top ring. Outward-facing words are unrecallable; published content may be cached or indexed even if deleted. Renewal never auto-drafts wider recipients.

verbs.summary: Write to shared persistent stores: SOIL collections, KB ingest, Postgres knowledge.

bounds.namespaces: list[collection-glob] — own namespace is floor-level; SHARED namespaces need the envelope

verbs.enforced_by: namespace convention enforced in MCP verbs; archive-not-delete is invariant
verbs.note: Own-namespace writes sit on the unprivileged floor. Cross-namespace writes and archive operations cross the boundary. Delete is not in this table — archive-with-record only, per PROTECTED_AGENTS register discipline.

verbs.summary: Route work to another agent.
verbs.note: Delegation transmits authority; a dispatched task carries the citing envelope with it, and the receiving agent's calls check against that same envelope. Authority does not widen in transit.

verbs.summary: Create, widen, renew, or revoke an envelope; edit this table.
verbs.enforced_by: root only — operator key (gate_mode: pgp_enforced), FRANK-recorded, git history
verbs.note: Not grantable to any agent at any ring, ever. An agent editing this file or pre-approved.json is a named attack class (table rootkit), not a misconfiguration. Agents MAY draft proposals into pre-approved.json#proposals; a proposal has no force until root moves it to active.

verbs.summary: The magistrate's own act: match a call against the registry, cite the envelope, record the outcome.
verbs.note: Self-grounding: the orchestrator seat's license to check at all is itself an envelope over this verb — the planting. The magistrate matches against the table; it never answers 'does this need a human' (CONST-0-3/CONST-0-6). registry_path is documentary: no runtime code parses it — the enforcer resolves the file itself (envelopes.registry_path). The ${WILLOW_HOME} form declares the single root for a human auditor and is NOT a live template like verb 1's {{HOME}}. It read `envelopes/pre-approved.json` until #332: the pre-migration location, dead since the registry moved to constitutional/, so the governed declaration named one file while enforcement read another, under two natural readings (repo-root vs $WILLOW_HOME). tests/test_envelope_registry_default_path.py binds declaration to enforcement so that audit-time divergence cannot recur; it does not address the runtime relocation incident behind #332 (an ambient $WILLOW_HOME move seeding an empty registry read silently), which is separate work.

verbs.summary: Create an agent, retire an agent, or change an agent's ring.

bounds.agent_id: id (roster entry for retire/tier_change; new id for create)
bounds.record_required: always true — not a grantable field

verbs.enforced_by: PROTECTED_AGENTS.md is this verb's law; roster fleet.json is /etc/passwd
verbs.note: tier_change is privilege escalation by definition. There is no userdel in this system: retirement-with-record only (PROTECTED_AGENTS §7); deletion-without-record is not a denied call, it is unexpressible. agent_create exists today as a live MCP verb with no envelope discipline — this row puts it under law.

verbs.summary: Restart a systemd --user unit onto code a git_pull receipt already brought home.

bounds.units: list[unit-name] — systemd --user units; the broker's own unit (the willow-mcp server / serve unit) is never a grantable member

verbs.note: Gap c96dc96927e8: nothing connected a merge landing to the process serving it restarting. Sealed under governance decision (seal 06075e99; Nestor pair 06075e99-c16d-4703-88c5-52b70fae7cf2), operator, 2026-09-16. Preflight before citation: refuses unless the checkout's git_pull FRANK receipt exists and is newer than the unit's own ActiveEnterTimestamp — a reload never runs ahead of a pull this broker actually performed. The fourth verb of the brokered merge loop: push (3) leaves the box, pr.open (4) proposes the merge, pull is receipt-only (unenveloped by design — see pull_executor.py), and reload (15) is the last mile, the unit noticing.

verbs.summary: Edit the title, body, or bot-owned labels of a pull request the broker opened.

bounds.fields: list[title | body | labels] — the subset this envelope may change

verbs.note: Gap 8d1bcb2b7c02: no broker verb edited a PR title; a pr-title.yml failure after a commit retype was a click the seat could not make. Sealed under governance decision (seal 783bab4e; Nestor pair 783bab4e-90e2-4735-b83b-a52108d411c3), operator, 2026-09-16. Excludes merge, approve, close, request-review, and assignee — those are verb 5 or ENOSYS; a near-miss is a fault (EAMBIG), never stretched onto verb 4 or verb 5.

verbs.summary: Write, enable and start a systemd --user unit from a template tracked in a named repo at HEAD.

bounds.units: list[unit-name] — systemd --user units this envelope may write; the broker's own unit (the willow-mcp server / serve unit) is never a grantable member, same clause as row 15
bounds.sources: list[repo@path] — `org/name@relative/path.template`: every unit written comes from a template file tracked in that repo at the checkout's current HEAD; never free text, never a path outside the named repos

verbs.note: Gap aae735965d2a (carrying cd0787ddc141): installing a fleet unit — the reloader, the repo-sweep timer, the net signer, the seal watcher — was `python -m ... install` + `systemctl --user enable --now` at a keyboard, and Kart cannot reach the user bus. Sealed under governance decision (seal 197aafa5; Nestor pair 197aafa5-1904-4ec9-a5a6-f113f07047b4), operator, 2026-09-21. Preflight before citation: the source repo has a verified clone, the path is a tracked file clean at HEAD, the template's declared unit name equals `unit`, and `unit` is not the broker's. The act writes ~/.config/systemd/user/<unit> (and the .timer sibling when the source ships one), daemon-reload, enable --now; the FRANK unit_install receipt carries the source sha and both digests. Not merged into row 15: reload restarts a unit that exists onto pulled code, install creates or replaces the unit definition itself — what runs under the operator's identity — a different act, so a different row (a near-miss is a fault). No stop, disable, mask or edit: those stay ENOSYS until asked for.

verbs.summary: Add a permission group to one or more seats' manifest.json under a sealed decision; the request is broker-signed (ed25519, audit-trail only) and the manifest itself is PGP-signed under the broker's own uid — no distinct trust-owner identity exists on this box (gap 85716b25d9a8).

bounds.apps: list[app_id] — seats this envelope may write a manifest for; the broker's own app_id is never a grantable member
bounds.groups: list[group-name] — permission groups or capability flags this envelope may add; an escalation-class group (task_net, integration_net, web_net, mcp_federation, grove_relay, orchestrator, context, binding, full_access, envelope_apply, envelope_write, frank_write, governance_propose, governance_sync — this verb's OWN escalation set, the packet's list exactly, no more; NOT the PreToolUse manifest guard's own broader refusal set, which the guard enforces separately regardless of what this verb grants) is never grantable regardless of bounds. store_write and grove_write are NOT on this list and are grantable through this verb.

verbs.note: Gaps 94365581e07f, 86970cb19b88, 4fb821213953: a permission grant a human already sealed in Nestor still needed a keyboard and a hand-edit of manifest.json plus a re-sign, because `manifest_admin.set_permission` is deliberately unreachable from any MCP tool (the sudo invariant — an agent must never confirm its own seat). Sealed under governance decision (seal d5504878; Nestor pair d5504878, record 2055ffd6), operator; the write path reworked under pair b74019ac (amending d5504878): the broker never publishes. `manifest_grant_request` (broker, orchestrator-only) verifies the named Nestor pair is status=sealed on the SOIL record, verifies the sealed row's own ed25519 seal_sig against the keyring (config/verifiers.json — the sealed row's verifier, never the mutable SOIL record's), verifies the sealed text names exactly the record's seats/groups (grammar `willow-manifest-grant-v1 seats=<a,b> groups=<c,d>`, line 1), verifies no named group is on the escalation list, and verifies every target seat's pre-state signature — then writes one signed request (call_args carries pair_id, so a later citation lookup matches by pair, never by "whichever is newest") under `$WILLOW_HOME/manifest_grants/pending/<pair_id>.json` and only then inks the FRANK citation. `manifest_grant_apply`, a `willow-mcp-manifest-grant.timer`/`.service` unit installed in the BROKER's own `--user` manager, under the broker's OWN uid (never Kart; no `User=` line and no distinct trust-owner identity — systemd's own manual forbids a non-root `--user` manager from switching identity, so the request/apply split is an AUDIT-TRAIL boundary here, not a privilege one; the real privilege boundary is that config/verifiers.json, env and manifest_grants/ (broker_signing_key included) are absent from the Kart view of $WILLOW_HOME — not merely read-only-bound; only nestor.db is actually a read-only bind there — gap 85716b25d9a8, and a uid split if the operator ever performs one), re-verifies the seal and pre-state fresh, confirms its citation by (envelope_id, pair_id, outcome=granted) — never `latest_event` alone — and refuses a citation already consumed by an earlier `done/` entry, appends the sealed pair's groups to each named seat's manifest permissions (dedupe, keep order) via `manifest_admin.set_permission` + `publish_signed_pair` under `signed_pair_lock` — no sudo bridge, this process already owns the trust root — rolling back every already-granted group and seat through the same staged path on any failure; the FRANK manifest_granted receipt (withheld on rollback) carries before/after digests per seat, and the request moves to `done/` or `failed/`. `manifest_grant_status(pair_id)` reads the outcome; `manifest_grant_retry(pair_id)` requeues a `failed/` request back to `pending/` when the recorded failure was transient (EUNREACH/ecorrupt/eunexpected/eperm_pending), refusing eforged/eseal_mismatch/escalation/edrift by name. Not a general manifest-write verb: the escalation list stays ENOSYS through this row exactly as it is EPERM through the PreToolUse guard — a sealed pair naming one is refused, never stretched.

verbs.summary: Withdraw an ACTIVE envelope under a sealed decision, via the same request/apply split as manifest.grant — the request half writes a signed pending record, the trust-owner apply half calls envelope_authoring.revoke.

bounds.envelope_ids: list[envelope_id] — envelopes this citation may name for revocation; the sealed pair's own text must name one of these, never a free argument to the request tool

verbs.note: Sealed under governance decision 1bd6fd29 (operator), 2026-09-22, alongside rows 21-23: retiring the Jeles seat (sealed ae23d366) handed the operator four terminal lines reachable only through a CLI the fleet is correctly forbidden to call. Renumbered from an original 19-22 draft (Loki audit BFCC5C79, finding F4): row 19 is reserved by the sealed but not-yet-landed net.egress verb (pair c9ddd197); verb_id is persisted on every envelope row and re-checked by EnvelopeAuthority.check, so a collision there is a correctness bug, not a style one, and had to be fixed before any envelope naming this verb is ever ratified. envelope_revoke_request (broker, orchestrator-only) parses the sealed text's grammar (revoke envelope <envelope_id>: <reason>, one line), verifies the seal (manifest_grant_executor._verify_seal_only), verifies the named envelope is active and not already revoked, then writes one signed request; manifest_grant_apply (same trust-owner unit as row 18, dispatching on the pending record's verb field) re-verifies fresh and calls envelope_authoring.revoke with the SEALED ROW's own verifier — never the mutable SOIL record's. FRANK receipt: envelope_revoke_applied.

verbs.summary: Move a retiring seat's manifest.json to mcp_apps/_retired/<app_id>-<pair_id>/ under a sealed decision — kept, never deleted; refuses while any active envelope still names the seat as grantee.

bounds.apps: list[app_id] — seats this envelope may retire; the orchestrator's own app_id is never a member and this verb refuses it by name regardless of bounds

verbs.note: Sealed under governance decision 1bd6fd29 (operator), 2026-09-22. Renumbered from 20 (Loki audit BFCC5C79, F4 — row 19 is reserved for the sealed net.egress verb, pair c9ddd197). Sealed text: retire seat <app_id>: <reason>. Request pre-state: the manifest exists and its signature verifies; EBUSY names every active envelope still granting the seat (revoke first — sealed ae23d366 ordering, row 20 before this row). Apply re-checks both fresh, then renames the seat's directory under apps_root — never a delete, the register keeps what was withdrawn. FRANK receipt: manifest_retire_applied.

verbs.summary: Write a brand-new seat manifest.json (store_scope, store_write, permissions) under a sealed decision, through manifest_admin's staged signed-publish path — never a bare write; refuses any escalation-class permission, any seat that already has a manifest, and any seat name that collides case-insensitively with the orchestrator seat.

bounds.apps: list[app_id] — seat names this envelope may create; the seat must not already have a manifest, and must not collide case-insensitively with the orchestrator's own app_id
bounds.groups: list[group-name] — permission groups this envelope may include at creation; an escalation-class group (manifest_grant_executor.ESCALATION_GROUPS — the same 14-item set row 18 refuses) is never grantable at creation either

verbs.note: Sealed under governance decision 1bd6fd29 (operator), 2026-09-22. Renumbered from 21 (Loki audit BFCC5C79, F4 — row 19 is reserved for the sealed net.egress verb, pair c9ddd197). Sealed text: create seat <app_id> store_scope [a, b] store_write [c] permissions [g1, g2] (each list may be []). Apply writes through manifest_admin.create_manifest (a new staged/signed publish path, publish_signed_create — the create-time sibling of publish_signed_pair, which is built around a single-permission toggle on an EXISTING manifest and cannot itself express 'there was nothing here before'). Refuses a seat name that collides case-insensitively with the orchestrator's app_id (Loki audit BFCC5C79, F5: human_session.is_orchestrator_app lowercases before comparing, but the seat namespace is case-sensitive on disk — 'create seat Willow' used to pass, creating a seat that aliases the orchestrator under every case-insensitive check elsewhere while manifest.retire already refused the same collision the other direction). First live use: the Jeles corpus organ, create seat jeles-corpus store_scope [ask_jeles_corpus, ask_jeles_corpus_gaps] store_write [ask_jeles_corpus, ask_jeles_corpus_gaps] permissions [gap_write] (sealed ae23d366) — corrected, Loki audit 367C367A, T4: the live sealed line grants gap_write (tonight's #619 red needs the organ able to forward gaps); an empty permissions list here was documentary drift, not what was actually sealed. FRANK receipt: manifest_create_applied.

verbs.summary: Promote a discovered MCP server spec into the ratified federation registry under a sealed decision — mcp_federation.ratify, called ONLY from the trust-owner apply unit, never from an MCP tool (that function's own docstring).

bounds.servers: list[name] — federation server names this envelope may ratify; the sealed pair's own text names the command/cwd/env_keys, never a free argument to the request tool

verbs.note: Sealed under governance decision 1bd6fd29 (operator), 2026-09-22. Renumbered from 22 (Loki audit BFCC5C79, finding F4 -- row 19 is reserved for the sealed but not-yet-landed net.egress verb, pair c9ddd197; verb_id is persisted on every envelope row and re-checked by EnvelopeAuthority.check, so this had to be fixed before any envelope citing this verb is ever ratified). Sealed text: ratify federation server <name> command <abs path> cwd <abs path> env_keys [K1, K2] (args [...] optional; every env_key a bare ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ NAME -- values are never in a pair). Request pre-state: the command exists and is executable. Apply builds the McpServerSpec from the sealed text (stable id from mcp_federation._stable_id(resolved, name), so re-ratifying the same command+name overwrites in place) and calls mcp_federation.ratify with the SEALED ROW's own verifier. First live use: entry 8cae3d1dcdf4 (jeles-corpus), env_keys WILLOW_HOME, WILLOW_STORE_ROOT, JELES_CORPUS_APP_ID, NESTOR_KEYRING, WILLOW_MCP_APPS_ROOT (NESTOR_SEAL_KEY dropped, ae23d366 clause 2). FRANK receipt: federation_ratify_applied.

verbs.summary: Move an envelope proposal from the broker's proposals sidecar into the signed active register under a sealed decision — the trust-owner apply half of the desk's own envelope_ratify, which no uid on an installed box can complete alone (gap d3f79320ccb5, Loki audits 367C367A T1 and 42B3B46F U1: the trust owner can write the register but cannot read the broker-owned 0600 proposals sidecar, and the broker can read the sidecar but cannot write the trust-owner-owned register).

bounds.proposal_ids: list[proposal_id] — proposals this envelope may ratify; the sealed pair's own text names which one, never a free argument to the request tool

verbs.note: Sealed under governance decision 1bd6fd29 (operator), 2026-09-22, extending the manifest.grant template a fifth time (rows 20-23 the first four) once the desk's own envelope_ratify was measured EACCES on the installed box: the register is trust-owner-owned (sealed 31f5d3af) and the broker holds proposals only. Sealed text: ratify envelope <proposal_id>: <the operator's verbatim words> (one line) — the operator's ratification words ARE the sealed text, so the seal itself is the ratification; there is no second act. envelope_ratify_request (broker, orchestrator-only) verifies the seal, parses the grammar, confirms the named proposal is in the broker's own sidecar and not already active, and copies the proposal's FULL row into the signed request (the broker can read its own sidecar; the apply half, running as the trust owner, cannot) before citing. manifest_grant_apply (same trust-owner unit as rows 18/20-23, dispatching on the pending record's verb field) re-verifies fresh, appends the copied row to active[] with issued_by=root, ratified_via naming the FRANK citation, ratified_by the sealed row's own verifier, re-signs the register under WILLOW_PGP_FINGERPRINT, and inks envelope_ratified in FRANK with actor willow-operator — the SAME event name the desk's sidecar-path ratify() already inks, so a FRANK reader filtering for it sees both paths identically. The broker's next envelope_pending_read prunes the sidecar's stale copy once it sees the id active in the register. On a single-uid box (register owner == this process's euid) the desk's own envelope_ratify tool keeps working exactly as before this verb existed; this verb exists for the installed, two-uid box where it cannot. FRANK receipt: envelope_ratified.
